title: The Panama's two floors, Glover Compton, and the hours
summary: Upstairs at the Panama she sang blues and jazz from 8 to 12 with pianist George Hall, with Bricktop, Cora Green and Mattie downstairs and Glover Compton at the piano.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: -- went up to the -- not we, just I, went up to the Panama. The Panama was upstairs. They had an upstairs and they had a downstairs. Now, Bricktop, Cora Green, Matty

And Glover Compton, Nettie Compton's husband, he was the pianist down there. He played piano. Sat there with a big cigar in his mouth, and just sat sideways. He never played, [Sitting occasionally] He sat this way all the time and played. Never looked at the piano keys. Never. He never even glanced at the piano keys.
Now, upstairs we sang the blues and all the jazz stuff and the real rough stuff. Not rough, but I mean the jazz and the blues.

And the people from all the downtown shows used to come up there, upstairs at the Panama, to hear us sing. There was nothing decorative about that, either. It was just a plain place. And a fellow named George Hall was the piano player upstairs, who could play a mess of piano.
What hours would this be that you performed there?
These were regular hours. What time did we start? About 8:00 o'clock? Yeah, 8:00 o'clock.
And how late would you go?
Worked till about 12:00. Yeah, till about 12:00. And then we'd go to the after hours places.
